name: DASH North American
summary: A week of hearty North American home cooking built around fruit, vegetables, beans, fish, low-fat dairy and unsalted nuts, with lots of flavour from citrus, vinegar, garlic, herbs and spice instead of salt. Chili, sheet-pan chicken, fish tacos and a Sunday roast, all low in sodium and saturated fat.
howItWorks:
**Flavour without the salt.** Lime, lemon and cider vinegar brighten most dishes. Garlic, onion, ancho chile and smoked paprika add depth, and roasting browns the edges. Six dishes get a pinch of salt, and that's all the salt in the week.

**Fruit, vegetables and the DASH way.** Fruit starts every breakfast, vegetables fill lunches and dinners, and there's low-fat milk or yogurt every day. Beans, oats, brown rice, unsalted nuts, potatoes, sweet potatoes and bananas bring potassium and fibre.

**Fish, and cook once, eat twice.** Seared salmon on Monday, almond-crusted trout on Wednesday and salmon tacos on Saturday bring omega-3, always cooked fresh. Monday's chili, Tuesday's chicken, Thursday's apple-sage chicken and Friday's red beans each make two portions, so the next lunch is done.

**Pick no-salt-added cans.** Look for "no salt added" on canned beans and tomatoes, "low sodium" on broth and "reduced sodium" on bread, and rinse beans anyway. Buy unsalted nuts.

**Light and Big.** The second snack drops away at Light, portions are smaller and there's less rice and tortilla. At Big the dishes grow and the snacks stay the same. If you take blood-pressure or heart medication, follow your care team's advice.

recipes.name: Blueberry banana overnight oats with walnuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Swiss Bircher muesli, by way of the North American overnight-oats jar
recipes.about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt until thick and creamy, then topped with blueberries, sliced banana, a little maple and toasted walnuts. It's a cold, grab-it breakfast made the night before. The **oats and fruit bring fibre and potassium**, and the milk and yogurt cover a good part of your dairy for the day.
steps: The night before, stir the oats, milk, yogurt, cinnamon and vanilla together in a jar or bowl. Cover and chill overnight.
In the morning, give it a good stir. If it's thicker than you like, loosen it with a splash of milk or water.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes.
Top the oats with the blueberries and sliced banana, then add the walnuts and a drizzle of maple.
recipes.tip: Frozen blueberries are great here: they thaw overnight in the jar and turn the oats a pretty purple. At Light, if it's loose, stir in a spoonful more oats or use less milk.

recipes.name: Blueberry and toasted oat parfait with almond crunch
recipes.inspiredBy: the classic diner-counter fruit and yogurt parfait
recipes.about: Thick Greek yogurt layered with juicy blueberries, a squeeze of lemon and a quick crunch of toasted oats and almonds, with a drizzle of maple and a pinch of cinnamon. It tastes like blueberry crisp for breakfast and comes together in minutes. The **Greek yogurt carries most of the protein**, and the blueberries bring fibre and vitamin C.

ingredients.note: a squeeze, to brighten the berries

steps: Toast the oats and almonds together in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden and fragrant. Tip onto a plate to cool.
Toss the blueberries with the lemon juice and half the cinnamon.
Stir the maple and the rest of the cinnamon into the yogurt.
Layer half the yogurt into a glass or bowl, then half the blueberries. Repeat, and scatter the crunchy oats and almonds on top just before eating so they stay crisp.
recipes.tip: Toast a double batch of the oats and almonds and keep them in a jar for the week.

recipes.name: Western-style veggie scramble with toast and orange
recipes.about: Scrambled eggs, cooked until set, with a splash of milk, sweet red pepper, onion and a big handful of spinach, seasoned with smoked paprika, thyme, garlic and black pepper, served with toast and a fresh orange. It's a diner Western omelette in scramble form, and the smoked paprika adds the smoky taste. The **orange brings vitamin C** and the eggs bring choline.
steps: Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 5 minutes, then stir in the smoked paprika and thyme for 30 seconds.
Add the spinach and cook until it wilts and the pan looks nearly dry, about 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the milk, garlic powder and pepper. Pour over the vegetables and stir gently with a spatula until completely set with no runny egg left, about 3 minutes.
Toast the bread. Serve the scramble with the toast and the orange wedges alongside.
recipes.tip: A little shredded cheddar is classic, but it adds sodium and saturated fat. This week, Tuesday is the morning with room for a small sprinkle.

recipes.name: Seared salmon and white bean salad with apple, celery and dill
recipes.inspiredBy: a deli-style salmon salad, lightened up
recipes.about: A seared salmon fillet flaked over baby spinach with creamy white beans, boiled egg, crisp celery and apple, in a lemony yogurt and Dijon dressing with plenty of dill. It's a quick lunch with crunch in every bite. **Salmon brings omega-3**, and the spinach brings vitamin A and folate.
steps: Lower the egg into a small pot of simmering water and cook for 8 minutes. Cool it under cold water, peel and quarter it.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, Dijon, half the oil, the dill and pepper together in a big bowl until smooth.
Add the celery, apple, onion and white beans and toss to coat.
Warm the rest of the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat and cook the salmon 3 to 4 minutes per side, until it flakes easily.
Pile the spinach on a plate, top with the bean salad and flake the warm salmon over it. Add the egg and eat right away, while the apple is crisp.
recipes.tip: Rinse canned beans well: it washes away a good share of the sodium.

recipes.name: Smoky turkey and two-bean chili
recipes.inspiredBy: classic North American chili, built on beans and lean turkey
recipes.about: A big pot of lean turkey, kidney beans and black beans in a thick tomato base with ground ancho chile, cumin, smoked paprika and a good squeeze of lime. The spices are toasted in the pot and the lime lifts everything at the end, so it tastes full with only a pinch of salt. It makes two bowls, so tomorrow's lunch is done, and the beans bring plenty of **fibre and potassium**.

ingredients.note: cooked ahead, or cook it while the chili simmers

steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 6 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Crumble in the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until well browned, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the ground ancho chile, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne and oregano and cook for 1 minute, until it smells toasty.

Add the tomatoes with their juice, about half a cup of water per portion (more if it gets too thick) and the salt. Bring to a simmer, then cook gently, partly covered, until thick, about 25 minutes. Meanwhile, cook the rice in plenty of simmering water, about 35 minutes, and drain.
Add both beans and simmer 10 minutes more. Take it off the heat and stir in the lime juice.
Ladle over the rice and top with cilantro. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
recipes.tip: It freezes beautifully. Double it and freeze single portions for busy nights. Cook a little extra rice too: it keeps 4 to 5 days in the fridge, ready for Thursday's bean bowl.

recipes.name: Sheet-pan lemon-herb chicken with potatoes and broccoli
recipes.about: Chicken thighs, potato wedges, carrots and broccoli roasted together with garlic, lemon, rosemary and thyme until browned at the edges. A little Dijon in the marinade gives it a tangy crust. It makes two portions, and the potatoes and broccoli bring **potassium** and vitamin C.

ingredients.note: cut in chunky wedges, skin on
from a lemon; zest it first

steps: Heat the oven to 220C (425F). Whisk the lemon juice, Dijon, half the oil, the garlic, rosemary, thyme, pepper and salt in a big bowl.
Toss the chicken in the marinade and let it sit while the oven heats, at least 10 minutes.
Toss the potatoes, carrots and onion with the rest of the oil on a large sheet pan. Roast for 15 minutes.
Move the vegetables over, tuck the chicken onto the pan and roast 15 minutes. Add the broccoli and roast until the chicken is cooked through and the edges are browned, about 12 more minutes.
Scatter the lemon zest over the top. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
recipes.tip: Leftovers reheat best in a hot oven or toaster oven, so the potatoes crisp up again. Making Big? Use two pans, so it roasts instead of steaming.

recipes.name: Almond-mustard baked trout with sweet potato and garlicky spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: New Orleans trout amandine, baked with a mustard and almond crust
recipes.about: Rainbow trout fillets with a crust of chopped almonds, Dijon and a little maple, baked until flaky, with roasted sweet potato and lemony garlic spinach on the side. It's a sweet and tangy crust that needs no salt. **Trout is an oily fish with omega-3**, and the sweet potato brings plenty of vitamin A.
steps: Heat the oven to 220C (425F). Toss the sweet potato wedges with two thirds of the oil and the pepper on a sheet pan. Roast for 20 minutes.
Stir the Dijon, maple, thyme, half the garlic and half the lemon juice together.

Push the sweet potatoes to one side and lay the trout on the pan. Spread the mustard mixture over the fillets, press the chopped almonds on top and roast until the trout flakes easily and the almonds are golden, about 12 minutes.

While the trout roasts, warm the rest of the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the rest of the garlic for 30 seconds, then the spinach with a splash of water, and toss until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Squeeze the remaining lemon over the spinach and the fish, and serve with the sweet potatoes.
recipes.tip: Cook it fresh: fish is best the day you bake it.

recipes.name: Southwest black bean and egg bowl with lime yogurt
recipes.inspiredBy: Southwest Tex-Mex flavours: lime, cumin, corn and black beans
recipes.about: A colourful bowl of black beans, sweet corn, avocado and spinach over brown rice, topped with a fried egg and a cumin and lime yogurt dressing. It's fresh, a little spicy and totally satisfying, and the yolk, cooked firm, breaks into the rice. The **beans and brown rice bring fibre**, and the avocado brings creamy healthy fat and potassium.
steps: Cook the brown rice if you don't have any ready: simmer in plenty of water until tender, about 35 minutes, and keep the extra in the fridge for the week (it keeps 4 to 5 days).
Whisk the yogurt, lime juice, cumin and ancho together with a spoonful of water until pourable.
Toss the beans, corn, onion and half the cilantro with a spoonful of the dressing.
Fry the egg in the oil in a nonstick pan until the white and the yolk are firm, about 4 minutes, flipping it for the last minute.
Pile the spinach in a bowl, top with the rice and the bean salad, then add the avocado, the egg and the remaining cilantro. Drizzle with the rest of the dressing.
recipes.tip: Use the extra rice from Monday's chili. Cooked brown rice keeps 4 to 5 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Apple-sage chicken with walnut brown rice and braised red cabbage
recipes.inspiredBy: Canadian harvest cooking: apples, cabbage and sage
recipes.about: Chicken breast medallions pan-seared with sage and Dijon, with sweet-tart apple and red cabbage braised in cider vinegar, and a nutty brown rice pilaf with toasted walnuts. It's an autumn Canadian plate. It makes two portions, and the red cabbage and apple bring **vitamin C and fibre**.

ingredients.note: cut in medallions about 2 cm thick

steps: Rinse the brown rice and simmer it in plenty of water with the thyme until tender, about 35 minutes. Drain and keep warm.

Meanwhile, rub the chicken with the Dijon, sage and pepper. Warm half the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and sear the chicken 4 minutes per side, in two batches if it crowds the pan, until browned and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F). Rest on a plate, and wash your hands, the board and the knife after the raw chicken.
In the same pan, add the rest of the oil and cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes. Add the cabbage, apple, broth, cider vinegar and the salt.
Cover and braise over medium-low heat until the cabbage is soft and the liquid is almost gone, about 25 minutes.

Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes and fold them into the rice. Slip the chicken back into the cabbage for the last minute to warm, and serve with the rice. Pack the second portion into a shallow container and into the fridge within 2 hours for tomorrow's lunch; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C.
recipes.tip: Store the chicken sliced on top of the cabbage so it stays moist. Cook extra rice tonight and set some aside before the walnuts go in, for Friday's red beans.

recipes.name: Louisiana-style red beans and brown rice with turkey and spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Louisiana red beans and rice, with turkey in place of the sausage
recipes.about: Red kidney beans simmered with onion, celery and red pepper (the holy trinity of Louisiana cooking, with red pepper in place of green), garlic, thyme, bay and smoked paprika, with crumbled turkey and a little sage standing in for the sausage and a splash of vinegar to wake it up, over brown rice with wilted spinach. It makes two bowls. The **beans and spinach bring folate, fibre and potassium**.
steps: Cook the brown rice in plenty of simmering water until tender, about 35 minutes, then drain. If you saved rice from Thursday's chicken, just warm it.
Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat. Crumble in the turkey with the sage and half the smoked paprika and cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Scoop it out.
Cook the onion, celery and pepper in the same pot until soft, about 8 minutes, then add the garlic, the rest of the smoked paprika, the thyme, bay and cayenne and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the tomatoes, the beans, the turkey, about half a cup of water per portion (a splash more as it simmers if it gets too thick) and the salt. Simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken it.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, about 2 minutes. Take out the bay leaf and finish with the cider vinegar.
Spoon over the rice. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
recipes.tip: Leftover beans thicken as they sit, so loosen with a splash of water. A few drops of hot sauce at the table is the Louisiana finish; check the label for sodium.

recipes.name: Chili-lime salmon tacos with crunchy red cabbage slaw
recipes.inspiredBy: Baja-style fish tacos, with seared salmon in place of fried white fish
recipes.about: Salmon flaked into warm corn tortillas with an ancho chile, cumin and smoked paprika rub, a crunchy lime-cilantro slaw, avocado and a yogurt crema. It's fish taco night with fresh, bright flavours. **Salmon gives you omega-3**, and the cabbage slaw brings vitamin C and crunch.
steps: Mix the ground ancho chile, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and oregano and rub it over the salmon.
Toss the cabbage, onion and half the cilantro with half the lime juice.
Stir the yogurt with the rest of the lime juice and a spoonful of water to make a pourable crema.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the salmon 3 to 4 minutes per side, until it flakes easily. Break it into big chunks.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, then fill with slaw, salmon and avocado. Drizzle with the crema and finish with the remaining cilantro.
recipes.tip: Set out the toppings and let everyone build their own. At Light, use two small street-taco tortillas, or pile everything over the slaw as a bowl.

recipes.name: Canadian split pea soup with garlic croutons
recipes.inspiredBy: Quebec soupe aux pois, with smoked paprika for the smoky note
recipes.about: A thick, golden soup of split peas, carrot, celery and onion simmered with thyme, bay and smoked paprika for a smoky taste. A splash of cider vinegar brightens it up and the garlic croutons add crunch. **Split peas bring fibre and folate**, and it freezes well.

ingredients.note: yellow if you can find them, rinsed

steps: Warm half the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery until soft, about 8 minutes, then stir in the garlic, smoked paprika and thyme for 1 minute.

Add the rinsed split peas, the broth, about 2½ cups of water, the bay leaf and the salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered and stirring now and then, until the peas have fallen apart, about 50 minutes. Add a splash more water if it gets too thick.
Meanwhile, toss the bread cubes with the rest of the oil, the garlic powder and a little pepper and bake at 190C (375F) until crisp, about 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf and stir in the vinegar and a good grind of black pepper. Blend a third of the soup for a creamier body if you like.
Ladle into a bowl, swirl in the yogurt and top with the croutons.
recipes.tip: Yellow split peas are the Quebec choice. Double the batch and freeze portions.

recipes.name: Sunday roast chicken with root vegetables and pan sauce
recipes.inspiredBy: a classic North American Sunday roast
recipes.about: Chicken thighs roasted over potatoes, carrots and broccoli after a rub of Dijon, sage, thyme and garlic, finished with a pan sauce stirred with more Dijon. It's the Sunday dinner that makes the whole house smell wonderful. The **vegetables bring potassium and vitamin K**, and the sauce uses low-sodium broth.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C (400F). Toss the potatoes, carrots and onion with half the oil in a roasting pan and roast for 20 minutes.
Rub the chicken with the rest of the oil, most of the Dijon, the garlic, sage, thyme, smoked paprika, pepper and salt.

Nestle the chicken on top of the vegetables and roast for 25 minutes in all, tucking the broccoli in around the edges for the last 12, until the chicken is cooked through (74C or 165F) and the vegetables are browned.

Move everything to a plate. Set the pan over medium heat, pour in the broth and vinegar and scrape up the browned bits. Let it bubble for a minute or two until it reduces a little, then whisk in the rest of the Dijon. Spoon the sauce over the chicken and vegetables.
recipes.tip: Thighs stay juicy, so don't roast them past 74C. If your roasting pan can't go on the burner, scrape the browned bits into a small pot with the broth and finish the sauce there.

recipes.name: Warm vanilla nutmeg milk with maple
recipes.about: Low-fat milk warmed with vanilla, a little maple and a pinch of nutmeg until steamy. It's cosy and comforting. **Milk brings calcium and potassium**, with only a little added sugar.
steps: Warm the milk with the nutmeg and maple in a small pot over medium heat, whisking now and then, until steaming.
Stir in the vanilla and pour into a big mug.

recipes.name: Fresh guacamole with baked tortilla chips
recipes.about: Chunky guacamole with ripe avocado, lime, onion and cilantro, scooped up with corn tortilla chips baked until crisp. The lime does the work salt usually does. **Avocado brings potassium and healthy fat.**
steps: Heat the oven to 200C (400F). Brush the tortilla wedges lightly with the oil, spread them on a sheet pan and bake until crisp, about 8 minutes.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice, onion, cilantro, pepper and cumin, leaving it a little chunky.
Serve the guacamole with the warm chips.
recipes.tip: Press the guacamole's surface with plastic wrap if you're making it ahead, so it stays green.

recipes.name: Apple slices with maple-ginger yogurt dip
recipes.about: Crisp apple slices with a creamy dip of Greek yogurt, a little maple, vanilla and a pinch of ginger. Sweet, cool and filling. The **apple's fibre and the yogurt's protein** keep you going until dinner.
steps: Stir the yogurt with the maple, ginger and vanilla until smooth.
Slice the apple and serve it with the dip.
recipes.tip: Squeeze a little lemon over the apple slices if you're packing them, so they stay bright.

recipes.name: Crunchy carrots and celery with rosemary white bean dip
recipes.about: Carrot and celery sticks with a creamy white bean dip blended with lemon, garlic, canola oil and rosemary. It's a fresh, crunchy snack with a bit of protein. The **beans make it filling** and add potassium, and the carrots add vitamin A.
steps: Blend or mash the white beans with the oil, lemon juice, garlic, rosemary and pepper, adding a spoonful of water until smooth.
Cut the carrot and celery into sticks and serve around the dip.
recipes.tip: The dip keeps 4 days in the fridge, so make a bigger batch.

recipes.name: Peppery boiled egg with sweet red pepper strips
recipes.about: Boiled egg halves dusted with black pepper, smoked paprika and a pinch of cayenne, with a squeeze of lemon and crunchy sweet red pepper strips on the side. It's peppery, bright and sharp, so you don't miss the salt. **Egg brings choline**, and the pepper brings vitamin C.
steps: Lower the egg into a small pot of simmering water and cook for 8 minutes, then cool it under cold water and peel.
Halve the egg, dust with pepper, smoked paprika and cayenne, squeeze the lemon over it and serve with the red pepper strips.
recipes.tip: Boil a few eggs at once and keep them in the shell in the fridge for up to 5 days.

recipes.name: Smashed avocado toast with lime and black pepper
recipes.about: Creamy mashed avocado on toasted reduced-sodium bread with lime juice and black pepper. It's a fresh, creamy snack that doesn't need any salt. **Avocado brings potassium and healthy fat.**
steps: Toast the bread until crisp.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice and pepper, spread it over the toast and finish with a little more pepper.

recipes.name: Yogurt with banana, walnuts and maple
recipes.about: Plain Greek yogurt with sliced banana, crunchy toasted walnuts and a drizzle of maple. It's a creamy, fruity snack. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3**, the banana brings potassium and the yogurt adds calcium.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes until they smell nutty, then chop.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the banana and walnuts and drizzle with maple and a dusting of cinnamon.

recipes.name: Orange wedges with toasted almonds
recipes.about: Juicy orange wedges with a handful of toasted unsalted almonds. Bright, sweet and crunchy. **Orange brings vitamin C** and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until they smell nutty.
Cut the orange into wedges and serve with the almonds.
